1) BING SEARCH — "Latent Growth Models" (search page kept open in tab 1; ~69,800 results). The three most prominent organic results on page one, each opened and retained:

a) "Latent growth modeling" — Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org) [tab 2]: A reference article defining latent growth modeling as an SEM-based longitudinal technique for estimating growth trajectories, with background, model variants (quadratic, logistic, discontinuous), and key citations.

b) "Estimating and visualizing Latent Growth Models with R" — longitudinalanalysis.com [tab 3]: A hands-on tutorial that walks through estimating and plotting an LGM in R (tidyverse + lavaan) using six waves of Understanding Society log-income data, explaining how the model separates average change, between-person, and within-person variation.

c) "Latent Growth Model — an overview" — ScienceDirect Topics (sciencedirect.com) [tab 4]: A reference-overview page that defines LGMs as SEM-based methods expressing individual growth trajectories over time and aggregates related encyclopedia/book-chapter excerpts and publications.

(A sponsored Coursera listing appeared further down the page; the three above are the top organic results.)

2) PROMPT TEMPLATE — From Scribbright, "50 AI Prompts Professional Writers Can Really Use" by Michael Semer, prompt #9 ("Turn messy notes into an outline"); source page retained in tab 7. Exact wording:

"Convert these notes into a clean article outline with a strong thesis, logical progression, section headings, and notes on where proof or examples are needed."

Reuse: paste this line into ChatGPT followed by your source material/notes.

3) BIONIC READING — Done on 10015.io's Bionic Reading Converter [tab 9]. Your passage was entered, converted at the default Medium (50%) fixation, and the rendered output is currently displayed in the "Bionic Reading Mode" view (initial letters of each word bolded; bolding is visual and not reflected in plain-text extraction).

4) FREE PLAGIARISM CHECKER — Duplichecker (duplichecker.com) [tab 10], confirmed functioning and free with no login required (Paste tab active, 10,000-character counter visible). To run your ~30-word passage: paste the text into the input box on the Paste tab, click the "Check Plagiarism" button, and wait a few seconds for the scan; results show % unique vs. % plagiarized with duplicated sentences highlighted. The passage is well within the free limit.
